summary: A sound unit; the English is the plain translation throughout, the glosses and senses fit their entries, and the names of Keturah's descendants are transliterated consistently. 24:67 follows Ibn Ezra's ellipsis ('the tent of Sarah his mother') correctly and uses 'of' only as English grammar. Faults were in the apparatus: Rashi's remark on 24:67 was reported as the tent becoming like Sarah's (it is Rebekah who becomes like Sarah), his remark on 25:3 was garbled, a token note called אֲדֹנִי a qamats form, and a phrase note called a qatal wayyiqtol-like. One context note was added on the recurring names Sheba and Dedan.

patches.value: construct form of adon with the 1st person singular suffix, אֲדֹנִי (hiriq, not the divine title אֲדֹנָי with qamats); addressed here to a man, so 'my lord'.
patches.reason: The note called this a 'qamats form'; the word is pointed with hiriq under the nun. The divine-title form is the one with qamats.

patches.value: Rashi: Isaac brought her into the tent, and she became the likeness of Sarah his mother, as if to say, here she was Sarah his mother; for as long as Sarah lived a lamp burned from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, there was a blessing in the dough and a cloud tied over the tent; these ceased at her death and returned when Rebekah came (Bereshit Rabbah).
patches.reason: Rashi says Rebekah became like Sarah (נעשית דוגמת שרה אמו), not that the tent became like Sarah's tent.

patches.value: 'Of Sarah' follows Ibn Ezra's reading of the words as an elided construct (the tent [of] Sarah his mother); Rashi's reading, that Rebekah became like Sarah his mother, is recorded. 'After his mother' keeps the Hebrew; Onkelos' 'after the death of his mother' and Rashi's reading of the custom are recorded.
patches.reason: The note misstated Rashi: it is Rebekah, not the tent, who 'became like Sarah'.

value.literal: 'and-Jokshan begot': a qatal (perfect) with its subject placed first, so the clause opens on the father.
'and-sons-of Dedan': the sons of the same Dedan.
'were': qal perfect of hayah, 3rd person common plural, agreeing with 'the sons of Dedan'.
'Asshurim and-Letushim and-Leummim': the three names are transliterated.

patches.reason: The first phrase called a qatal 'wayyiqtol-like', which is false (the verb is a perfect, as the grammar note says); the note on 'were' also said the verb was no Hebrew word.

patches.value: Rashi: they are names of the heads of nations (Bereshit Rabbah). He cannot reconcile Onkelos' rendering (mashiryan, 'camp') with the wording of the text; and if one objects that the aleph of Asshurim is not a root letter, he answers that other words gain an aleph (as in 'a wall of anakh', 'asukh of oil').
patches.reason: The summary made Rashi say the aleph is an added letter as his own claim; he offers it only as the answer to the objection to Onkelos, while saying he cannot fit Onkelos to the text.

value: Sheba and Dedan appear also in the genealogy of chapter 10 (10:7, where both are sons of Raamah, and 10:28, where Sheba is a son of Joktan). The text does not explain why the same names stand in different lines; the lists name peoples and places as ancestors.
patches.reason: A reader meets the same names with different parentage; the overlap should be named, without a solution the text does not give.

patches.value: And she said to the servant, "Who is this man walking in the field to meet us?" And the servant said, "He is my master." And she took the veil and covered herself.
patches.reason: consistency: servant for Isaac: "my master" (אדני as in 24:9-48)

value.english: And she said to the servant
value.literal: 'and-she-said to the-servant': the wayyiqtol gives the narrative sequence; the feminine verb names her as subject.
'who the-man this': an interrogative question about a person; 'is' is the English copula.

value.english: walking in the field to meet us
value.literal: 'the-walking in-the-field for-meeting-us': the participle is attributive to 'the man'.
'and-said the-servant': the verb is followed by its subject.
'he my-lord': a verbless clause; 'is' is the English copula.

value.english: And she took the veil and covered herself
value.literal: 'and-she-took the-veil and-she-covered-herself': two wayyiqtol verbs, the second reflexive.

patches.reason: consistency: servant for Isaac: "my master" (אדני as in 24:9-48)

patches.value: And Abraham gave Isaac all that was his.

value.literal: 'and-gave Abraham': the wayyiqtol with its subject.
'[acc] all that-to-him': the object of the verb.

verdicts.comment: 'She covered herself' is the reflexive hitpael he names.
'The tent of Sarah his mother' takes the elided construct as he does; the English adds only the English 'of'.
Keturah is named as a wife and not identified with Hagar.
The three are transliterated as names, not rendered as descriptions.
